Zoë, great week. You completed all four sessions, and the 1500m continuous swim on Sunday with no stops is exactly the kind of work that builds toward your race. I liked seeing "last two felt smooth" on Monday too, since smooth usually means your stroke is holding up under fatigue. Sleep came up to 7.6 hours and your HRV trend improved, so your body is responding well to the load. Open water at 17 degrees is no joke, so well done getting in for that Wednesday session. Keep it steady this week.

Mei-Ling

Thảo, good week. You got on the overhang wall Monday, which is exactly the kind of terrain that builds toward a 5.11 outdoors, and you made it to 3 of 4 sessions. Sleep came up to 7.1 hours from 6.7, and your recovery trends stayed steady.

I'm sorry to hear about your right shoulder aching since Wednesday's climb, and I'll reach out to talk about it.

Kwame

Ngozi, great week. You finished all three Reformer sessions, and the footwork series finally clicking on Thursday is exactly the kind of progress that sticks. Trying the jumpboard for the first time on Saturday took some nerve too.

Sleep came up to about 7.4 hours a night and your daily steps climbed to around 9,200, so your body had more to work with. Your heart rate and HRV have stayed steady, which is a good sign that your recovery is keeping pace with the work.

Keep going with the same rhythm next week, and let me know how the back stiffness feels as you settle into it.

Ines

Björn, four for four this week, and holding 1:52 splits across the 6 x 500m was solid, controlled work. Your 2k test came in at 8:04, which tells me you're close to where you want to be. Sub-8 is within reach, and the next few weeks are about turning that near miss into a clean one.

Sleep edged up to 7 hours, and your recovery trends have held steady, which is exactly what we want while you push the pace. Keep the consistency going, and we'll work out the pacing for the next 2k together.

Henrik

Aisha, you finished all four sessions this week, and that's a strong week for someone working on stress and sleep. The two yin sessions and the breathwork walk look like exactly the kind of recovery work you're after, and the "almost fell asleep in pigeon" note tells me you were properly relaxed. Sleep came up to 7.8 hours on average, and your resting heart rate and HRV both trended the right way.

Keep an eye on that evening wind-down, since it seems to be working. I'll see you at the next session.

Rafael

Hiroshi, nice work getting two sessions in this week. The Monday 5k steady piece and the Friday rate pyramid both got done, and you noted the rate 28 felt hard, which is useful information for building your rowing back up. The Wednesday intervals didn't happen, and that's fine. Two of three in a week is a solid base to build on.

Your sleep and steps both edged up on last week, and your recovery trends have held steady. Keep the same approach next week and we'll look at adding that interval session back in.

Siobhán

José, thanks for the honest note about work. The one session you did this week was Monday's 40-minute hatha yoga, and you flagged tight hamstrings, which is useful for us to know as we work on your flexibility goal. Sleep averaged 6.3 hours, a little under last week, and your HRV dipped slightly, so it makes sense that the week felt heavy. No need to make up the missed sessions. Just pick one short session you can fit in this week and we'll build from there.

Mei-Ling

Fatima, great week: you got all three sessions done, including the 55 km outdoor ride on Sunday, which is a real step toward that 100k. Fading in the last 10k tells us something useful about pacing and fueling, and we can work on that together. Your sleep held steady at about 7 hours, and your resting heart rate stayed steady too, while HRV dipped a little, so keep an eye on how you feel over the next few days.

Kwame

Dmitri, nice work in the pool this week. You got both swims done, and the Friday session of 20 x 50m with tight turns is solid, focused work that builds real swimming fitness. Your sleep and steps also edged up from last week, and your recovery trends have held steady, which tells me the load is sitting well with you.

Keep the twice-a-week swims going and let's see how the next week feels.

Henrik

I'm going to reach out to you directly to talk about how you're doing, and I want to hear from you soon.

Keep the sleep and steps moving the same way, and we'll check in on your leg numbers Thursday.

Keep building toward that V5. Next week, let's look at how your campus work feels as you add load. Proud of this one.

Mateus, strong week. You finished all five sessions, and Sunday's 10k came in at 46:10, nine seconds faster than September. That's real progress toward sub-45. The Monday intervals stand out too, since you kept working through a hard third 2k.

Sleep averaged 7.4 hours, up from 7.1, and steps rose to 10,200 a day. Your heart rate and HRV trends stayed steady. Let's keep building from here, and I'll check in on the next block.

Kwame

Ayşe, great week. You finished all three workouts, and moving up to the 16 kg kettlebell on Monday is a real step in strength. Your incline hike on Wednesday is exactly the kind of time on your feet that will carry over to hiking season. Sleep came up to an average of 7 hours and your steps rose too, and your recovery trends are heading the right way, which should help with the energy you want at work.

Keep an eye on those lungs-burning sprints on Friday; that's a sign the intervals are working, and we can adjust the pace next week if you want.

Tomasz
